ch03.anchor: Rear a tiger and you leave yourself a calamity
ch03.note: The proverb yang hu yi huan (养虎遗患), 'rear a tiger and bequeath yourself trouble,' from Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian: Zhang Liang and Chen Ping warn Liu Bang that to let his rival Xiang Yu go unstruck would be 'to keep a tiger and leave oneself a calamity.' Chen's point is that sparing Wang Jingwei loosed just such a tiger—the Nanjing puppet regime.

The essay Zuihou zhi xinqing (最后之心情), presented as Wang Jingwei's deathbed confession. Its authenticity is disputed: the text did not surface until 1964, some twenty years after his death, reaching a journalist rather than his family; the hand is not clearly Wang's, and his widow Chen Bijun denied that any such testament existed. Chen relays the received account; historians have never settled whether the piece is genuine.
